archive_start.speaker: narrator
archive_start.text: By the time Lin Yue reached the northern receiving house, summer dust had become a stain inside her collar. She set down her ordinary pack and asked for water before asking for work. The clerk pointed her toward a shaded basin. Nothing in her recent travels had given her ownership of the roads ahead. She carried a sword, clean practice leads, clothes that needed mending, and a notebook with more blank leaves than she had expected to keep.

archive_01_002.speaker: narrator
archive_01_002.text: The notice stood between a carpenter's apprenticeship offer and the price of winter millet. A mountain archive needed paid help moving records away from a leaking roof. Its seal promised neither an examination nor a recovered treasure. Three lines named carrying, copying and observing treatment under qualified direction. A fourth warned that some rooms would remain closed. Yue read that line again. A place willing to advertise the work it would not permit seemed worth asking about.

archive_01_003.speaker: lin_yue
archive_01_003.text: I have four opened pairs, and I can use the bounded controls for which I have been examined. I cannot dry a wall by declaring it part of my practice. If you need someone to read lists, move a sound box over checked ground, or test an approved small socket, I can discuss those tasks. If the notice means recovering every damaged word, I should leave it for another applicant, because I do not know anyone who can honestly promise that.

archive_01_004.speaker: narrator
archive_01_004.text: The receiving clerk did not look impressed by her stage. He turned the notice over and showed its countersignature. The appointment ran for thirty-six calendar days, including rest days, at five copper each day. Outward fare was eight copper; another eight remained reserved for the return. Meals and a shared dry sleeping place belonged to the appointment. Beyond that term, any continued work required a new agreement. He placed a plain tally beside the impressive seal.

archive_01_005.speaker: narrator
archive_01_005.text: Yue asked what happened if the weather prevented useful carrying. The clerk found the answer rather than offering reassurance from memory. Paid waiting within the agreed term stayed paid. Nobody had hired her to keep a mountain pass open. She copied the clause into her notebook and felt, briefly, absurd for being so pleased by it. Then a porter beside the stove asked the same question about his own notice. The clerk handed him the tally without changing his voice.

archive_01_006.speaker: narrator
archive_01_006.text: Outside, the porter divided his lunch between two cloths. One portion would go to a daughter working in the soap yard. He offered Yue a piece of onion bread after confirming that it contained no fish paste. They ate on the receiving house's stone threshold while carts passed in both directions. He said he had carried dry records before, and wet ones were heavier for reasons that had nothing to do with their words. Yue watched him tie the empty cloth.

archive_01_007.speaker: narrator
archive_01_007.text: The archive cart left the following morning. Its driver inspected the brake in front of the passengers and refused a merchant's last bundle because the listed load had already been reached. The merchant complained that paper weighed less than grain. The driver asked whether he meant the dry paper in the bundle or the copper clasps holding it shut. After a silence, the merchant arranged a second journey. Yue climbed aboard without offering to make the first one carry more.

archive_01_008.speaker: narrator
archive_01_008.text: The road rose through terraces where bean vines had begun to yellow. At a turning, the driver stopped beside a shrine whose roof had been replaced with plain boards. No invitation asked travelers to admire the repair. A woman was sweeping water out of the doorway and argued with him about the cart's wheel grease. They had known one another long enough to make the argument useful. Yue held the brake while he checked the rim she had noticed.

archive_01_009.speaker: narrator
archive_01_009.text: During the pause, Yue examined the cuff seam on her practice coat. Its conducting stitch stayed folded away from the ordinary carrying straps. Having earned more internal routes had enlarged her possible tasks; it had also enlarged the number of mistakes she could arrange through an ill-placed lead. She made no test on the roadside. The coat needed an ordinary needle first. The driver handed her one from his repair box, then returned to the wheel without watching her work.

archive_01_010.speaker: narrator
archive_01_010.text: At noon they reached a bridge laid against a fixed stone ridge. The mountain did not hover above its farms or depend on a visitor's reserve to remain there. Water ran beneath the span through a cut lined with old masonry. A mason tapped the outer course, listened, and marked one section for a later inspection. The driver took the inner line she permitted. Yue noticed that nobody asked the mason to explain the entire mountain before accepting her narrow instruction.

archive_01_011.speaker: narrator
archive_01_011.text: The first archive roofs appeared beyond a stand of black pines. They were lower than Yue had imagined. Smoke came from a kitchen chimney; laundry hung under the eaves of a caretaker's house. Above those ordinary things, a square tower carried a bell without gilding. The driver said it marked opening, supper and a closed road. He described the three meanings before mentioning the tower's age. Yue found that order sensible and knew enough of herself to mistrust her immediate approval.

archive_01_012.speaker: narrator
archive_01_012.text: A young courier waited by the unloading platform with a board tucked under one arm. He asked the driver for the actual arrival interval, then crossed out the interval someone had predicted. His coat had faded to a colour somewhere between lake water and old ash. When a carrying strap slipped, he corrected it without letting the board fall. He did not introduce himself until the cart stood on its chocks. 'He Xi,' he said. 'The paid unloading crew is over here.'

archive_01_013.speaker: narrator
archive_01_013.text: The platform's guide line ended before a shallow patch of broken paving. He Xi explained that the line marked the checked route, not a convenient place to store extra boxes. Two workers took the merchant's bundle from the cart with a sling. Yue carried her own pack and the driver's folded receipt. She had arrived hoping to be useful. For the first few minutes, being useful meant staying out of the work already assigned to people who knew its corners.

archive_01_014.speaker: narrator
archive_01_014.text: Tan Ke met them at the inner door carrying a wooden tray. Its contents were mostly empty: clean cloth, a short ruler and two wedges. Her sleeves were rolled above elbows mottled with old paper dye. She looked at Yue's sword, then at the bench beside the door. 'Secure it there during room work,' she said. 'A turning body should not bring a metal point over somebody's wet page.' Yue obeyed before explaining that she already knew the danger.

archive_01_015.speaker: tan_ke
archive_01_015.text: If you already know a rule, that saves us time. It does not mean I should be ashamed to say it. I will keep repeating the rules when a room changes, because a familiar room is where people stop noticing their hands. Today you may carry the empty supports. Tomorrow you may have permission for a particular box. Your appointment is not a general key. The inventory will tell you what its keeper has actually entrusted to us.

archive_01_016.speaker: narrator
archive_01_016.text: The inner corridor smelled of pine boards, damp cloth and cabbage. Yue followed Tan past doors with different coloured tags. Blue meant ordinary access; red meant structural closure; a tied white tag meant the room's contents required a separate keeper. Tan insisted the colours were accompanied by written words because dusk and poor sight could turn a useful sign into a guess. At the final door, an older woman had added the closure word in larger script herself.

archive_01_017.speaker: narrator
archive_01_017.text: Dai Shuren stood behind that door rather than opening it at once. Her silver hair was pinned so tightly that Yue could see the pull at her temples. An ink-dark finger rested on the admission list. She compared Yue's receiving tally with its retained counterpart, including the fare entry. Only then did she introduce herself as chief custodian. The delay felt cold until Yue saw a visitor's rejected copy beside her elbow, bearing a nearly identical but incomplete seal.

archive_01_018.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_01_018.text: I do not expect visitors to enjoy this part. Some have crossed a long road and think a keeper's first duty is to reward the crossing. Mine is to know which work I have asked for and which sources I am permitted to place before you. A false admission paper is not a false person. It can still put a person in a room whose owners never agreed to admit them. We begin with the paper because its mistake is smaller than that mistake.

archive_01_019.speaker: narrator
archive_01_019.text: Yue asked whether the rejected visitor had been sent away without supper. Dai looked up sharply, then opened a second page. Shelter and the public waiting bench required no admission to the guarded rooms. The visitor had eaten and could correct his application through the receiving house. 'I wanted that answer before I praised the checking,' Yue said. Dai's finger moved from the admission list to the shelter line. For the first time, the keeper seemed to consider Yue herself.

archive_01_020.speaker: narrator
archive_01_020.text: They signed the thirty-six-day appointment in the public office. Dai read the five-copper rate aloud, named the weekly rest place, and confirmed that weather waiting did not become an unpaid debt. Yue asked who received an injury report. Tan wrote her own name for immediate practical limits and the village clinician's for assessment. Dai added that stopping unsafe work could not cancel already earned wages. The clerk gave Yue a copy small enough to fit inside her habitual notebook.

archive_01_021.speaker: narrator
archive_01_021.text: Luo Zhimo arrived halfway through the signature. He carried six returned reading slips and had tucked a wooden bookplate into his belt where a sword might have hung. His greeting to Dai contained an argument before it contained Yue's name. Two visitors had waited all morning for a charter copy that still lay in a closed room. Dai said the room had a roof beam moving above it. Luo said he had asked for yesterday's certified copy, not a climb beneath the beam.

archive_01_022.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_01_022.text: If the certified copy already exists, withholding it protects no beam. The people waiting have a departure cart at dusk. Their harvest boundary hearing will not pause because we have correctly discovered a cracked roof. I accept the closure. I do not accept using the closure to answer every request that passes through the office. Let Tan tell us what can move. Let the copy list tell us what is already outside. Then refuse the thing that actually needs refusing.

archive_01_023.speaker: narrator
archive_01_023.text: Dai took the slips from his hand and read the numbers. One requested copy was present in the public cabinet. The other had been prepared but not countersigned. She released the first and retained the second for the comparison it lacked. Luo accepted that division without continuing the quarrel. Yue had expected a fight between generosity and caution. Instead she saw two people disagreeing about an inventory. Their voices made the difference louder than it was; their next actions made it precise.

archive_01_024.speaker: narrator
archive_01_024.text: Tan showed Yue the public cabinet after the visitors collected the admitted copy. Its shelves carried originals that owners had made public, certified copies with named comparison dates, and working transcriptions marked for checking. Each category had a separate place. The cabinet was not arranged by beauty or age. A rough copy from last month might be more usable for a present request than a magnificent roll nobody had permission to read. Yue began drawing the arrangement, then asked before copying any visible headings.

archive_01_025.speaker: narrator
archive_01_025.text: At the far table, a girl watched a clerk read her employer's wage agreement. She had chosen to hear the payment and notice clauses, leaving a personal guarantee covered. The clerk pointed with a blunt reed rather than a knife tip. When the girl asked whether refusing to renew would make her dishonest, he reread the notice period instead of giving her a moral answer. Yue set her notebook down. There were rooms in which observation itself could become another uninvited audience.

archive_01_026.speaker: narrator
archive_01_026.text: Tan led her away before the reading continued. In the corridor she said the public room did not turn every reader into a public exhibit. Visitors could observe the room's arrangement; hearing a person's chosen consultation required that person's permission. Yue had been about to write down the girl's question as a useful example. She crossed out the identifying detail she had already begun. The blank left behind was awkward, and she let it remain awkward rather than repairing it with an invented anonymous speaker.

archive_01_027.speaker: narrator
archive_01_027.text: The archive's meal bell sounded while they were still in the corridor. Workers set their gloves and outer wraps on a rack before entering the kitchen. A cook checked that everyone had washed, including Dai, whom she called by a childhood name. The chief custodian surrendered her authority with surprising speed at the basin. Luo had already found a seat beside the open shutter. Tan chose the bench where she could stretch her knees without moving anyone's bowl.

archive_01_028.speaker: narrator
archive_01_028.text: He Xi brought the last pot from the stove, but the cook stopped him when he began serving. His unloading shift had ended. A kitchen worker took the ladle and sent him to eat. He sat opposite Yue with his board still beneath one arm. She asked whether the board needed a place of its own. He laughed, looked embarrassed, and leaned it against the wall. For the first time since the cart arrived, both his hands were available to hold his bowl.

archive_01_029.speaker: he_xi
archive_01_029.text: I keep thinking someone will need one more thing entered before I finish. Usually someone does. My mother says a courier who carries every last question never reaches a destination. She was speaking about deliveries, but I think the remark fits supper. The board belongs to the unloading account. I can put it down because another worker has the next shift. That sounds obvious when I say it. It has taken me longer to learn than the road to this kitchen.

archive_01_030.speaker: narrator
archive_01_030.text: Yue told him she had once kept a practice sheet beside her food until an older worker moved it out of reach. He Xi asked whether the worker had been right. She said the answer depended on whether she finished eating before defending herself. Their laughter remained small enough not to disturb the cook's instructions. At the other end of the table, Dai and Luo discussed the visitor's uncertified charter. Even in an argument, they passed the cabbage between them without hesitation.

archive_01_031.speaker: narrator
archive_01_031.text: After supper, the rain began as a tapping on the kitchen's outer sill. Tan set a cup beneath a small drip and told the cook it was a roof report, not a permanent repair. The cook pointed to the list already beside the pantry door. Three people had written the same leak on different days. Tan added the present interval without claiming the previous entries meant anyone had done nothing. The work order carried a carpenter's next visit; the cup would need emptying before then.

archive_01_032.speaker: narrator
archive_01_032.text: The sleeping room held four bed spaces divided by hanging cloth. Yue's space had a dry shelf and a peg for her coat. A worn notice listed quiet hours and the person who could change sleeping arrangements. She checked the floor before setting down her practice case. Outside, someone dragged a bucket over stone. Her body wanted to follow the sound and become useful again. Instead she unfolded the blanket. The archive had hired a worker whose next morning required sleep.

archive_01_033.speaker: narrator
archive_01_033.text: At dawn, the rain had left a pale seam along the eastern wall. Yue ate before meeting Tan at the inspection bench. She showed the retained stage-five practice record she habitually carried, then kept its personal pages closed. Tan asked which permitted task the record supported today. Yue answered that it did not decide the roof's safety. They would first use ordinary levels and the carpenter's report. A cultivation result could remain true without being the answer to the first question asked of it.

archive_01_034.speaker: narrator
archive_01_034.text: The practice bench had an isolated grounded socket maintained by the archive's qualified operator. The operator named its purpose: checking a small stop signal, with no connection to heaters or guarded papers. Yue could decline the test and still take ordinary tasks. She chose a blank comparison within her recovered allowance, using only an established route and a measured small command. They recorded expenditure and discharge. Neither the bench nor her fourth opened pair became permission to force an unknown document dry.

archive_01_035.speaker: narrator
archive_01_035.text: When the check ended, Yue felt the familiar disappointment of a result too quiet to impress anyone. The operator was looking at the closure mark, not her face. He handed her a cloth for the lead and asked whether ordinary hand sensation had changed. It had not. That answer went onto the practical task list. Her realm stayed where her examination had placed it. Today's work would spend reserves, attention and meals; it would not become a new stage because the building needed saving.

archive_01_036.speaker: narrator
archive_01_036.text: Tan unlocked a tool chest with two workers present. It contained support boards, clean linen, weights, narrow brushes and empty receiving sleeves. She counted each kind before giving Yue a tray. Supplies issued for one room did not become a wandering personal kit. A broken brush might matter less than a missing document, but both needed a place in the day's account. Yue wrote the issue number on the tray's paper tag. He Xi copied it into the transport list without taking the original away.

archive_01_037.speaker: narrator
archive_01_037.text: They inspected the eastern corridor from its dry end. A carpenter stood behind the red closure cord and used a long rule to show where a roof joint had slipped. Nobody stepped beneath the beam to confirm what his tool already made visible. He would need two more workers and a supported roof interval before opening the bay. Rain on the tiles complicated the work. Tan entered those requirements beside the closure rather than reducing them to a promise that the carpenter would come soon.

archive_01_038.speaker: narrator
archive_01_038.text: Inside the adjoining sound room, a line of boxes had absorbed damp along their lower corners. Their keepers' inventory numbers stayed legible. Tan did not open them to see whether a damaged page might make a better story. She checked the issued moving permissions against each number and sorted the boxes into two rows. Five could move to the dry workroom under existing terms. Three required contact with their owners or a specifically recorded emergency decision. Yue placed no private source into the convenient row.

archive_01_039.speaker: tan_ke
archive_01_039.text: A closed box can tell us that its wood is wet. It cannot tell us that every paper inside is wet, or that opening it is the only useful response. We can move a permitted box above the floor, record its condition and ask its keeper what treatment they allow. Where immediate damage makes waiting impossible, the emergency clause names who may decide and what they must report. We will read that clause before we need it, because panic is a poor way to discover an agreement.

archive_01_040.speaker: narrator
archive_01_040.text: One permitted box was heavier than its outer size suggested. He Xi stopped the lift and fetched the listed sling. Yue held the support tray while two assigned carriers moved the load along the checked corridor. Her qi remained quiet. The box had survived a leaking roof and did not need an apprentice's untested carrying trick added to its history. At the workroom, Tan checked the seal and wrote the new shelf location beside the old one, keeping both visible.

archive_01_041.speaker: narrator
archive_01_041.text: The second box had a weak bottom board. They slid a rigid support beneath it before lifting and left the damaged board's fragments in a labelled sleeve. A clerk suggested replacing the bottom at once so the receiving shelf would look orderly. Tan refused until the keeper had approved the replacement and its record. Yue could see why the suggestion was attractive. The broken wood made everyone feel careless. Preserving the evidence of that carelessness was a different task from preserving the box's appearance.

archive_01_042.speaker: narrator
archive_01_042.text: Luo came with the two visitors' charter request after the carriers had finished. The unchecked copy lay in his own wrapper, separate from the boxes. He wanted to know whether its original could be reached without entering the closed bay. Tan checked the location list. It could not. Another certified copy might exist at the district receiving house. Luo asked for a messenger allowance to look for that copy. Dai authorized the bounded inquiry and wrote that it did not certify the unchecked paper already here.

archive_01_043.speaker: narrator
archive_01_043.text: Yue offered to compare the copy's visible public headings with the inventory. Dai permitted that narrow task while keeping the charter's private account annex covered. The copy named a cultivation terrace, a public path and a harvest boundary. Its certification space was blank. Yue wrote that blank into her note instead of quietly treating the seal on the wrapper as a seal on the contents. Luo watched her do it and admitted he had almost allowed the wrapper to answer a question it could not hear.

archive_01_044.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_01_044.text: The people outside will ask why an older official seal is not enough. I could tell them seals have different jobs, and they might think I am hiding behind a lesson. I need an answer they can use. If the district copy was compared before this roof failed, it may support their hearing. If no such copy exists, we should say when a safe comparison could happen and what provisional statement our own record actually warrants. Delay must have a receiving address, not merely a respectful tone.

archive_01_045.speaker: narrator
archive_01_045.text: Dai drafted a note stating that the charter's presence in the archive inventory was confirmed, while the unchecked transcription's accuracy remained unconfirmed. It was less than the visitors wanted and more than a refusal. Luo took it outside with the explanation of the district inquiry. Yue stayed in the workroom. She had no permission to turn the visitors' disappointment into a private interview, and no reason to believe her sympathetic face would improve the note's actual authority.

archive_01_046.speaker: narrator
archive_01_046.text: Rain thickened before the noon bell. The light at the workroom window grew yellow under the oiled cloth screen. Tan moved the lamp farther from the supported pages and changed its angle. Yue asked whether a small permitted light would help. Tan said an ordinary lamp already supplied what they needed; the difficult part was keeping heat away. They measured the distance with the issued rule. A useful reserve could remain unspent when the apparatus had a simpler safe arrangement.

archive_01_047.speaker: narrator
archive_01_047.text: The first box they opened held public school accounts. Its keeper had permitted the inventory check and gentle separation of loose covers, but not chemical treatment or reconstruction of missing entries. Tan read the permission aloud before cutting the wrapper's outer tie. Yue watched the cut ends drop into the issue tray. They would stay with the day's handling note. He Xi recorded the opening interval and the names present. Nobody used the school's public purpose to enlarge the offered treatment.

archive_01_048.speaker: narrator
archive_01_048.text: A smell like old leaves rose from the box. Several book covers had curled, but the upper register lay dry enough to support without unfolding. Tan showed Yue how to lift the whole supported bundle rather than grasp a tempting corner. The corner bore a child's name. Yue found her hand choosing it before her attention caught up. She moved her fingers back to the support board. A name could call to a person without making that person the right one to touch it.

archive_01_049.speaker: narrator
archive_01_049.text: The school register's list stopped halfway down a leaf. No flourish closed it. He Xi thought the missing lower names might have faded in the damp. Tan asked him to look at the numbering first. The following leaf continued the list, with the same interval in the heading. What appeared unfinished was a page turn. He Xi laughed with relief, then looked ashamed of the laugh. Yue said relief belonged in the room too. They kept the original sequence intact and placed the supported leaves together.

archive_01_050.speaker: narrator
archive_01_050.text: Beside the register lay a petition to fund roof tiles for the schoolhouse. It carried three signatures and one thumb mark. The petition's public covering clause allowed the archive to show its request; a private household annex stayed tied. Yue could report that the school had asked for tiles and what response the council recorded. She could not infer every signer's means from the presence of a mark. Luo arrived just in time to hear that distinction and asked to use it in the public catalogue note.

archive_01_051.speaker: narrator
archive_01_051.text: Tan allowed the catalogue note after checking the school's stated scope. Dai required the note to identify the petition as a request, not an approved expenditure. The council's later response was still in another permitted bundle. Yue wrote the two locations separately. A teacher looking for an answer could follow them; a reader admiring the first page would not accidentally declare the roof paid for. The difference made the catalogue longer. Luo said the extra line was worth more than another elegant heading.

archive_01_052.speaker: narrator
archive_01_052.text: In the afternoon, Sun Nian entered with a stick whose handle had worn smooth under her palm. The clerk offered her the nearer chair without asking whether she could reach the farther one. She chose the nearer chair anyway. Her left eye was clouded, and her right searched for the petition's wrapper number. She had copied that request when she worked at the school. Dai asked whether she wanted to see the public covering page or speak about a separate subject. Sun said she wanted to begin with tea.

archive_01_053.speaker: narrator
archive_01_053.text: They carried the tea to the public consultation alcove. Tan left the petition supported in its own tray; familiarity did not remove its handling limits. Sun rested her stick against the table and asked whether Yue was the new preservation worker. Yue described her bounded tasks. Sun listened, then asked how many people had told her that this archive contained the village's memory. Yue said three, if she counted the cart driver's joke. Sun smiled. 'Count that one carefully. Drivers remember practical things.'

archive_01_054.speaker: sun_nian
archive_01_054.text: A village does not put all its remembering in one building. We keep some in cupboards, some in habits and some in people who would rather not be asked this afternoon. I copied school lists for thirty years. The lists can tell you who was entered, not every child who sat beneath the window. If you ask me about those mornings, I may offer an account. That account still comes from this person sitting here, with an eye that tires and tea that needs drinking.

archive_01_055.speaker: narrator
archive_01_055.text: Yue asked whether the archive had requested testimony from Sun. Dai had sent an invitation, which Sun had not yet accepted. The petition's surviving cover raised a question about a teacher's unpaid materials, and Sun might know which account should be requested next. She did not want to tell the story before understanding who would hear it. Luo brought the proposed audience list. It included the school trustees and the named receiving clerk, not every visitor attracted by an old witness.

archive_01_056.speaker: narrator
archive_01_056.text: Sun crossed out the phrase village assembly on the draft. She would discuss the materials account at a bounded school meeting first. Publication of an extract would require another answer after she saw the wording. The clerk prepared a revised invitation rather than treating her corrections as an acceptance. Sun folded it and placed it inside her own sleeve. Yue noticed how carefully she did that. An invitation could look like a small official fact while remaining a question whose answer had not arrived.

archive_01_057.speaker: narrator
archive_01_057.text: As Sun left, He Xi held the outer door against the wind. She called him by his mother's name first, corrected herself, and waited for him to answer. He did not pretend the mistake had been nothing. 'I have her carrying straps,' he said. 'My face is my father's argument.' Sun laughed, then grew quiet at the mention of his father. She offered no explanation. He Xi let the door settle after her and returned to the workroom with both hands empty.

archive_01_058.speaker: narrator
archive_01_058.text: Yue did not ask what the silence meant. He Xi had been introduced as a paid courier, not as an unfinished family story available to the new worker. Instead she asked whether the day's transport list needed her signature. He brought it over and pointed to the two movements she had actually witnessed. A third movement belonged to another crew. She signed only the first two. The small refusal of a convenient signature felt connected to the larger refusal of a convenient question.

archive_01_059.speaker: narrator
archive_01_059.text: At the evening report, Tan laid out the school bundle, the closed boxes and the roof closure as separate matters. The supported register needed continued observation. The school petition needed its response account. The three unopened boxes needed permissions or a properly invoked emergency decision. The roof needed a carpenter's supported interval. Dai approved the next day's tasks by number. Luo asked which public requests could proceed without those tasks. Their meeting took longer than the rain's loudest spell.

archive_01_060.speaker: narrator
archive_01_060.text: One clerk wanted a single notice saying preservation had begun. Luo agreed to the heading but rejected a claim that every affected record was now safe. Tan named the work completed and the uncertainties still present. Dai added the public request address and the emergency contact. Yue copied the final notice in large plain script. She had made enough beautiful mistaken copies in her training to understand why the clerk looked disappointed when she refused to fill the margin with a decorative cloud.

archive_01_061.speaker: narrator
archive_01_061.text: They posted the notice beneath the outer shelter. A farmer read the roof closure first, then asked whether his boundary request was among the records moved. The clerk checked his number without letting him inspect another visitor's slip. His record was in a dry room. Its ordinary queue remained unchanged. He was pleased for a moment, then annoyed that an emergency had not moved him ahead. Yue heard both feelings and had no reason to improve either one into gratitude.

archive_01_062.speaker: narrator
archive_01_062.text: At supper, the cook announced that the pantry's eastern wall would need checking before more grain was stacked against it. Dai tried to postpone the matter until the roof crew arrived. The cook asked whether the roof crew could prevent rats from reaching a damp sack tonight. Tan volunteered a limited inspection after eating. She would not stay into the next shift without changing its account. Dai listened, then named the kitchen worker whose paid evening duty could join her.

archive_01_063.speaker: narrator
archive_01_063.text: Yue offered to carry sound sacks during that inspection if her remaining agreed hours allowed it. Tan checked the task list rather than accepting the offer automatically. Two ordinary carrying turns remained within Yue's day; after those she would stop. The kitchen worker would supervise the destination and issue count. He Xi's shift had ended, and he stayed at the table. The account did not turn friendship or concern into invisible extra carriers. Yue finished her food before moving the first sack.

archive_01_064.speaker: narrator
archive_01_064.text: The pantry inspection found moisture along the outer boards but no wet grain inside the two issued sacks. They moved the sacks onto the inspected inner pallet and left the rest untouched until the morning count. The cook marked the locations on her pantry chart. Yue had expected the rescue of paper to feel different from the rescue of millet. Her arms made no such distinction. Both tasks required supports, named keepers and a person willing to notice when the load had changed.

archive_01_065.speaker: narrator
archive_01_065.text: When the two turns ended, she washed her hands at the kitchen basin. The water darkened with ordinary dust. Tan asked about sensation in her fingers and soreness from carrying. Yue reported both without making the report a cultivation verdict. The clinic would assess any worsening limit; tonight she needed rest and the meal she had actually eaten. Tan released her from the workroom instead of rewarding her honesty with one more supposedly easy task.

archive_01_066.speaker: narrator
archive_01_066.text: On the way to bed, Yue passed the public cabinet and found Luo checking a copy beneath the ordinary lamp. He had another worker's countersignature waiting space beside his own notes. She asked whether he was still on a paid shift. He showed her the evening rota with some embarrassment. She said she had meant the question for his sleep, not his virtue. 'They look similar when somebody asks at a doorway,' he answered, and set the lamp's shutter before continuing.

archive_01_067.speaker: narrator
archive_01_067.text: In her room, Yue wrote the day's completed tasks on her retained appointment sheet. She kept the cultivation practice entry separate. The stage-five result did not turn the pantry sacks into an examination; the sacks did not cancel the value of a recovered closure. She had been trying to make the two pages justify one another. Now she let them lie side by side without an arrow between them. Through the outer wall came the sound of rain entering a bucket someone had agreed to empty.

archive_01_068.speaker: narrator
archive_01_068.text: Morning brought no dramatic change. The roof still leaked, the closed room stayed closed, and the supported school register had not become a restored book overnight. Tan checked its condition before changing the linen beneath it. She explained that the first day's success was a page remaining where they had placed it, with no new tear. Yue had slept well enough to find that result satisfying. She wondered how long satisfaction would last when an owner asked for the page's missing lower corner.

archive_01_069.speaker: narrator
archive_01_069.text: The corner belonged to a different school account, not the register they had kept intact. Its remaining lines showed a materials advance to a teacher named in the public response. A later note mentioned repayment, but the amount lay across the damaged edge. Dai permitted an exact transcription of visible public fields and required the gap to remain marked. Luo fetched the school's retained comparison copy. If it preserved the amount, they could compare its scope without pretending the wet original had healed.

archive_01_070.speaker: narrator
archive_01_070.text: The retained copy arrived in a wrapper signed by the school trustees. It had been compared four years earlier, before this roof damage. Its amount was readable. Tan placed it on a separate dry table, away from the original's treatment tray. The copy could support a practical inquiry into the old payment. It could not replace the damaged object's physical history. Yue drew two columns in her notebook and named the difference rather than using the easier word complete above both.

archive_01_071.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_01_071.text: A useful copy does not insult an original. An original does not make every copy worthless. What frightens me is the sentence that puts one in the other's place without telling the reader. When a person asks what was paid, this compared copy may answer within its authority. When a person asks what happened to the old leaf, the torn leaf is still here. We will preserve the copy's comparison date and the leaf's present condition, even if a neater catalogue would prefer one object.

archive_01_072.speaker: narrator
archive_01_072.text: Luo asked Dai whether the copy could go to the trustees' meeting before the roof repair. She agreed to a permitted extract of the payment and response clauses, with its comparison provenance. The private annex stayed outside the meeting. He Xi offered to carry the extract during his next paid route if the address was confirmed. Dai wrote the receiving trustee's name and asked for an acknowledged handover. A sealed packet could travel without recruiting the courier as a witness to everything inside it.

archive_01_073.speaker: narrator
archive_01_073.text: Yue watched He Xi copy the address, then hesitate at its last line. The trustee's office stood beside a house whose gate carried his family name. Dai noticed the hesitation too and asked whether the route presented a conflict he wished to declare. He said it might. His own inheritance petition concerned a different account kept here. He could carry the public school extract without reading it, but he wanted another worker to check the handover so nobody later joined the two matters through his surname.

archive_01_074.speaker: narrator
archive_01_074.text: Dai accepted the declaration and assigned the route's ordinary second check. She did not remove He Xi from every task as if disclosure made him untrustworthy. Luo thanked him for giving the office a practical question before it became a rumour. He Xi looked relieved and then annoyed at his relief. Yue recognized the feeling. A person could be grateful for a fair response while still resenting the habit of expecting an unfair one.

archive_01_075.speaker: he_xi
archive_01_075.text: My petition is mine to offer when I am ready. Today I have told you enough to arrange the delivery properly. I have not asked for a hearing while I carry your boxes, and I do not want every work list to acquire a note about my father. Please keep the conflict notice with the route account. If I ask you to read the petition later, we can decide who should be present then. A paid day does not have to contain the whole family.

archive_01_076.speaker: narrator
archive_01_076.text: Dai wrote exactly that scope on the route account. The petition itself remained in the guarded receiving cabinet, unopened for today's work. Yue had not seen it and made no note about its contents. At the public door, a visitor asked He Xi whether the archive was hiding an inheritance. He answered that it was holding a paper he had not authorized for public reading. Luo intervened only to explain the ordinary request procedure. He did not turn the question into a defence of the whole building.

archive_01_077.speaker: narrator
archive_01_077.text: By noon, the rain had stopped long enough for the carpenter to inspect the roof from its supported exterior walkway. Tan remained below at the marked receiving station. The crew would remove one damaged tile course after securing the beam, not pull the entire roof open to make the repair appear decisive. They could complete the temporary cover if the weather held. A full structural repair required a separately priced interval and materials the archive had not yet bought.

archive_01_078.speaker: narrator
archive_01_078.text: The carpenter's assistant sent down a split batten in a rope cradle. Tan labelled it with its roof position and observed condition. Yue carried the supported sample to the dry inspection table. She did not hold it as if the whole cause of the leak must fit inside one piece of wood. The carpenter described several contributing joints and the water's present route. Dai entered the temporary cover as a temporary cover. Luo asked what date the next inspection needed, rather than what word would make the notice reassuring.

archive_01_079.speaker: narrator
archive_01_079.text: On the outer steps, Sun Nian returned the revised invitation with one further correction. The trustees could hear her account of the materials request, but not a separate conversation she had held with the teacher's sister. She had chosen to withhold it after considering the audience overnight. Dai accepted the narrower answer. Sun said she would bring her own notebook to the bounded meeting and decide which entries could be examined there. Nobody asked to take it now merely because its existence sounded useful.

archive_01_080.speaker: narrator
archive_01_080.text: Yue offered Sun the sheltered bench while the clerk prepared her accepted scope. Sun chose to remain standing for a moment because her knee felt easier that way. The offer had been reasonable; the answer was still hers. Outside, a courier tested his cloak clasp and a worker shook rain from a ladder cover. Yue began to see how much of the archive's day consisted of people declining small conveniences. Each refusal saved a detail that a larger helpful story might have stepped over.

archive_01_081.speaker: narrator
archive_01_081.text: The school trustees' reply arrived before the afternoon carrying turn. They accepted the bounded meeting and supplied a list of four attendees. Luo posted the meeting time without posting Sun's home address. Dai kept the original invitation and her corrections together. Tan returned to the supported account leaf. Its edge had curled less under the measured room conditions, but the missing corner remained missing. The agreed conversation would not grant their tools a new power over that absence.

archive_01_082.speaker: narrator
archive_01_082.text: At the end of the second day, Yue stood beneath the repaired temporary cover and listened to an ordinary thin rain. Most of it now reached the gutter. One line still entered the receiving bucket at the far joint, which the carpenter had left on the next work order. The building had improved without becoming safe in every room. Inside it, a witness had accepted one audience, a courier had kept another paper private, and a copy had acquired a useful place beside an injured original.

archive_01_083.speaker: lin_yue
archive_01_083.text: I wanted to know on arrival whether I could help save an archive. That question was too large for the work I had actually been offered. Today I can name a supported page, an admitted copy, an unanswered roof joint and a meeting whose witness chose its limits. Tomorrow each will need people who remember those limits after the first relief fades. I have four opened pairs and one ordinary notebook. Neither should make me ashamed of writing the smaller answer.

archive_01_084.speaker: narrator
archive_01_084.text: Dai read the day's final handling list with her spectacles hanging from their plain bronze chain. Luo waited beside her with the school meeting notice. Neither looked triumphant. The cook called through the doorway that supper would cool while they improved each other's handwriting. Dai signed the completed movements; Luo left the unresolved request spaces blank. They went toward the kitchen together. Yue followed after washing the ink from her fingers, leaving the archive's ordinary rain to its gutters and agreed buckets.
